headline: Khelafat Majlis questions political deal behind President's resignation
summary: The party demands a fair investigation into allegations against former President Md. Sahabuddin, asserting that resignation alone is not enough.
details: Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis has raised questions about whether a political arrangement was behind the resignation of former President Md. Sahabuddin.

In a joint statement, party leader Maulana Mamunul Haque and Secretary General Maulana Jalaluddin Ahmad stated that Sahabuddin lost his moral and political legitimacy following the fall of the fascist government during the July uprising.

The party noted that while various groups demanded his resignation, the BNP initially created an environment to keep him in office, only changing its position later, which sparked suspicions of a political deal.
Khelafat Majlis also criticized the former President's contradictory statements regarding the resignation of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, questioning his neutrality and constitutional duty.
The party is now calling for a transparent and judicial investigation into allegations of abuse of power, constitutional violations, and involvement in financial scandals related to the S Alam Group.
They emphasized that the people of Bangladesh seek justice rather than political compromises, demanding exemplary punishment for those found guilty.
caption:
Was there a secret political deal behind the President's resignation? Khelafat Majlis demands a full trial.

Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis has raised questions about whether a political arrangement was behind the resignation of former President Md. Sahabuddin.

In a joint statement, party leader Maulana Mamunul Haque and Secretary General Maulana Jalaluddin Ahmad stated that Sahabuddin lost his moral and political legitimacy following the fall of the fascist government during the July uprising.

The party noted that while various groups demanded his resignation, the BNP initially created an environment to keep him in office, only changing its position later, which sparked suspicions of a political deal.

Khelafat Majlis also criticized the former President's contradictory statements regarding the resignation of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, questioning his neutrality and constitutional duty.

The party is now calling for a transparent and judicial investigation into allegations of abuse of power, constitutional violations, and involvement in financial scandals related to the S Alam Group.

They emphasized that the people of Bangladesh seek justice rather than political compromises, demanding exemplary punishment for those found guilty.

headline: Saudi prince died from drug overdose in London luxury hotel
summary: Abdullah bin Fahad bin Abdullah bin Abdulaziz bin Jalawi Al Saud, 29, was found dead in a Marriott hotel room in Kensington
details: Abdullah bin Fahad bin Abdullah bin Abdulaziz bin Jalawi Al Saud, a 29-year-old member of the Saudi royal family, was found dead in his hotel room at the Marriott Hotel in Kensington, West London, on November 25 last year.
A post-mortem report revealed that his death was caused by a mixture of alcohol and GHB (gamma-hydroxybutyrate), a known 'party drug'.

Toxicology reports presented in court showed 222 mg per 100 ml of ethanol in his blood, a level far exceeding the UK's legal driving limit of 80 mg, which experts say can cause unconsciousness or coma.
Lethal doses of GHB were also found in his body, along with cannabis, alprazolam (Xanax), and other medications.

Court documents indicate that the prince had a history of struggling with alcohol and Xanax addiction. He had previously been admitted to the Priory Clinic in Southwest London in August last year for detoxification from alcohol, benzodiazepines, and pregabalin.
